key_insight: Human and LLM collaboration produced comparable synthesis success rates and enabled discovery of a new material prototype, Ba3PtO5, in a closed-loop experimental workflow.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that combining expert judgment with LLM-generated synthesis recipes can accelerate materials discovery by improving candidate exploration and experimentally validating viable reaction paths.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper candidate materials using both humans and LLMs.
Tested recipes in the lab and fed results back into a closed-loop collaboration process.
Compared success rates across two rounds to assess performance on known vs. unknown targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental success rates of 83% vs 75% for known materials and 17% vs 22% for unknown materials in round one, with similar trends in round two.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply for unknown materials, so real-world deployment still depends on careful experimental validation and domain expertise.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
